summary: CCC Camp 734 is said to have built the tower in 1933-34; an 85-foot steel tower is listed for 1939-41; a towerman was hired in 1943; current condition is not described.

facts.design: Steel tower, about 85 feet tall (per a 1939-41 state annual report)

access.note: The NPS says visitors to the Big Spring Historic District can hike, picnic and camp. No source says whether the tower itself may be climbed.

events.note: Camp 734 built a fire tower in the park's southwestern corner, Nov. 1933 to Apr. 1934, per the historical marker. A March 1934 newspaper item still describes initial steps toward building one.
Missouri Conservation Commission annual report for 1939-41 lists an 85-foot steel tower
A garage mechanic took the towerman position at Big Spring State Park after the previous towerman resigned and moved to St. Louis
State official manual (1947-48) lists the towersite as owned by the Missouri Conservation Commission and located in the state park
Missouri State Park Board transferred ownership of three parks to the National Park Service; the NPS article does not name the three
Big Spring Historic District listed on the National Register of Historic Places; the district includes CCC-era features, among them a fire/lookout tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The marker dates Camp 734's tower work to Nov. 1933 to Apr. 1934; a March 1934 item describes only initial steps; a 1939-41 report lists an 85-foot steel tower. The story gives all three and does not choose a completion date.

The brief lists Big Spring State Park as the agency. The lookout history site names the Missouri Conservation Commission as owner in 1947-48, and the NPS says the state park board transferred three parks to the NPS in 1969 and now presents the cultural landscape as part of Ozark National Scenic Riverways. The story reports both; the brief's agency field is not changed.

notes_for_editor: Build date is unsettled: the marker says Camp 734 built the tower Nov. 1933 to Apr. 1934, the March 1934 item describes only initial steps, and the 1939-41 report lists an 85-foot steel tower; the sources may describe one tower or two. Current condition and climbing status were not found in any source I could open. A Semissourian article (ranger tour of a wildfire tower near Van Buren, found in search) returned HTTP 403 and is not used. Agency needs a check: the brief says Big Spring State Park; the NPS page says the state park board transferred three parks to the NPS in 1969 without naming them. The NPS sentence listing the fire/lookout tower with 'largely non-extant' features is ambiguous for the tower itself. The NHLR and firetower.org pages for this tower were not in the cache.
